question:
A series is given with one term missing. Select the correct alternative from the given ones that will complete the series.

? , TI, QC, NW, KQ, HK, EE, BY
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. WO.

GIVEN

• ? , TI, QC, NW, KQ, HK, EE, BY

SOLUTION

• 1st letters: ?, T, Q, N, K, H, E, B decrease by 3 → T(20)+3 = W(23).

• 2nd letters: ?, I, C, W, Q, K, E, Y decrease by 6 (cyclic) → I(9)+6 = 15 = O.

• Missing term = WO.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

SHORT TRICK

• Read the series backwards: each first letter +3 and each second letter +6 from the next term. From TI → W and O.

NOTE

• Fix A=1 … Z=26; treat each column of a two-letter series independently and note its common difference.

question:
A series is given with one term missing. Select the correct alternative from the given ones that will complete the series.

AT, YQ, WM, UH, SB, QU, OM, ?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. MD.

GIVEN

• AT, YQ, WM, UH, SB, QU, OM, ?

SOLUTION

• 1st letters: A, Y, W, U, S, Q, O, ? decrease by 2 (cyclic) → O(15)-2 = 13 = M.

• 2nd letters: T, Q, M, H, B, U, M, ? — gaps grow -3, -4, -5, -6, -7, -8, -9 → M(13)-9 = 4 = D.

• Missing term = MD.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

SHORT TRICK

• First column is a simple -2 chain; the second column has an increasing negative gap, so subtract 9 from OM's M.

NOTE

• When a column's difference is not constant, check for an arithmetic pattern in the differences themselves.

question:
Select the option that is related to the fourth letter cluster in the same way as the first letter cluster is related to the second letter cluster and fifth letter cluster is related to sixth letter cluster.

OE : LZ :: ? : PY :: XH : UC
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. SD.

GIVEN

• OE : LZ :: ? : PY :: XH : UC

SOLUTION

• Relation (1st→2nd): 1st letter -3, 2nd letter -5. Check XH→UC: X(24)-3=U, H(8)-5=C. ✓

• The pair is ? : PY, so ? = (P+3)(Y+5) = P(16)+3=19=S, Y(25)+5=30-26=4=D.

• Missing cluster = SD.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

SHORT TRICK

• To reverse the rule, add back: first letter +3, second letter +5 to PY → SD.

NOTE

• In A : B analogies, first find the fixed shift B←A, then apply the inverse to get the unknown.

question:
In the following question, set of letter clusters are given. The letter clusters of each set are related to the letter clusters of the same set by some Logic/Rule/Relation. From the given alternatives, select a group of letter clusters which follows the same Logic/Rule/Relation.

(WK, TF, QA)

(IL, FG, CB)
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. (DK, AF, XA).

GIVEN

• (WK, TF, QA) and (IL, FG, CB)

SOLUTION

• In each set: 1st letters fall by 3, 2nd letters fall by 5. WK, TF, QA: W→T→Q (-3), K→F→A (-5). Same for IL, FG, CB.

• Test options — Option 4: D→A→X (-3, cyclic) and K→F→A (-5). ✓

• Options 1, 2, 3 break the -3/-5 rule.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

SHORT TRICK

• Only check the step between the three clusters: first letters must drop 3 each, second letters 5 each.

NOTE

• For 'same rule' set questions, extract the internal step of the sample set and match it, not the values.

question: What was the day of the week on 26 March 2006?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. Sunday.

GIVEN

• Date = 26 March 2006.

SOLUTION

• 1 January 2006 was a Sunday.

• Day number of 26 March = 31 (Jan) + 28 (Feb) + 26 = 85th day.

• (85 - 1) mod 7 = 84 mod 7 = 0, so it falls on the same day as 1 Jan = Sunday.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

SHORT TRICK

• From a known anchor (1 Jan 2006 = Sunday), just add the day-count mod 7; 84 is a multiple of 7 → same day.

NOTE

• 2006 is not a leap year (28 days in February); odd-day counting is the fastest calendar method.

question: 7th of a month is Wednesday. This month has 30 days. What will be the 14th of next month?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. Friday.

GIVEN

• 7th = Wednesday; month has 30 days.

SOLUTION

• 7, 14, 21, 28 are Wednesdays. 30th = Wed + 2 = Friday.

• So 1st of next month = Saturday.

• 14th of next month = Saturday + 13 days = Saturday + 6 (13 mod 7) = Friday.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

SHORT TRICK

• Same date 7 days apart repeats the weekday. 30th is 2 days after the 28th (Wed) → Fri, so next-1st = Sat; 14th = Sat+6 = Fri.

NOTE

• Always reduce day-gaps by mod 7 to jump between dates quickly.

question: What was the last day of the year 1989?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. Sunday.

GIVEN

• Last day of 1989 = 31 December 1989.

SOLUTION

• 1 January 1990 was a Monday.

• 31 December 1989 is one day before that = Sunday.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

SHORT TRICK

• 31 Dec of a year = (1 Jan of next year) minus 1 day. 1 Jan 1990 = Monday → 31 Dec 1989 = Sunday.

NOTE

• 1989 is a non-leap year; 365 days = 52 weeks + 1 odd day, so each date advances one weekday the next year.

question: 5 persons P, B, C, G and H are sitting around a circular table facing towards the centre (not necessarily in the same order). B is sitting to the immediate left of C. Neither G nor H is the immediate neighbour of C. H is sitting second to the right of P. Who is sitting to the immediate left of B?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. H.

GIVEN

• 5 persons P, B, C, G, H face the centre. B is immediate left of C; G and H are not neighbours of C; H is 2nd to the right of P.

SOLUTION

• C's neighbours = B (left) and one more; since G, H are excluded, C's right neighbour = P.

• So clockwise: P, C, B, then the last two seats hold H and G.

• H is second to the right of P → H takes the seat two places right of P, leaving G at the end.

• Clockwise order: P, C, B, H, G. Immediate left of B (next clockwise) = H.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

SHORT TRICK

• 'Facing centre' → left = clockwise. Fix C-P first (only P can neighbour C), then slot H by the 'second-right' clue.

NOTE

• For centre-facing circles, immediate-left means the next seat clockwise; reverse it for outward-facing.

question: Diameter of 6 circles A, B, C, D, E and F is compared. No two circles have same diameter. Diameter of A is more than only E. Diameter of C is more than F but less than B. Diameter of D is not more than F. Diameter of how many circles is more than F?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. 2.

GIVEN

• A > only E (A is 2nd smallest, E smallest). F < C < B. D < F.

SOLUTION

• Smallest is E, then A (A greater than only E).

• D < F, and A is below D too, so order becomes: E < A < D < F < C < B.

• Circles greater than F = C and B = 2.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

SHORT TRICK

• 'More than only E' pins A at rank 2; then D and A both sit below F, leaving just C and B above F.

NOTE

• Convert every statement into a single '<' chain; ranking questions become instant once the line is built.

question: Two figures given on the left side of (::) are related with some logic/rule/relation. Select the missing figure on the right side of (::) from the given alternatives based on the same logic/rule/relation.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. the box reading 6, 5, 4, 2.

GIVEN

• [L, N, B, U] : [N, L, U, B] :: [5, 6, 2, 4] : ?

SOLUTION

• From figure 1 to figure 2 the entries swap in adjacent pairs: positions 1↔2 and 3↔4 (L,N,B,U → N,L,U,B).

• Apply to 5, 6, 2, 4: swap (5,6)→(6,5) and (2,4)→(4,2) = 6, 5, 4, 2.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

SHORT TRICK

• Just interchange the top two and the bottom two entries of the third box.

NOTE

• In figure-matrix problems, first spot the positional operation (swap/shift/rotate), then repeat it on the query figure.

question: Two figures given on the left side of (::) are related with some logic/rule/relation. Select the missing figure on the right side of (::) from the given alternatives based on the same logic/rule/relation.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. a square holding a plain square and a double (concentric) triangle side by side.

GIVEN

• Fig 1: square → triangle → concentric circle (nested). Fig 2: square holding a plain triangle and a concentric circle side by side.

SOLUTION

• Rule: the outer shape becomes the container and the inner shapes are un-nested, placed side by side; the doubled (concentric) inner shape keeps its double outline.

• Fig 3 is a concentric square containing a concentric triangle. Un-nesting gives a container square holding a plain square + a concentric triangle side by side.

• This matches Option 2.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

SHORT TRICK

• 'Open up' the nesting: outer boundary = box, inner shapes line up inside, and whichever shape was drawn twice stays double.

NOTE

• For figure analogies, track (a) nesting vs. side-by-side and (b) single vs. double outlines separately.

question: Two figures given on the left side of (::) are related with some logic/rule/relation. Select the missing figure on the right side of (::) from the given alternatives based on the same logic/rule/relation.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. the triangle filled with three '&' symbols.

GIVEN

• Hexagon : hexagon filled with 6 dots :: triangle : ?

SOLUTION

• Rule: the polygon is filled with as many symbols as it has sides. A hexagon has 6 sides → 6 dots.

• A triangle has 3 sides → it must be filled with 3 symbols.

• Only Option 4 shows the triangle with 3 '&' symbols.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

SHORT TRICK

• Count sides = count of inner marks. 3-sided triangle needs exactly 3 marks.

NOTE

• When a shape gets 'filled', check if the count of fillers equals sides, vertices, or a fixed number.

question:
Select the option that is related to the third letter-number cluster in the same way as the second letter-number cluster is related to the first letter-number cluster and sixth letter-number cluster is related to fifth letter-number cluster.

(NOTE: Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking down the numbers into its constituent digits. E.g.13 – Operations on 13 such as adding /subtracting /multiplying etc. to 13 can be performed. Breaking down 13 into 1 and 3 and then performing mathematical operations on 1 and 3 is not allowed)

LW200 : YJ100 :: DG180 : ? :: KP210 : RI105
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. IB90.

GIVEN

• LW200 : YJ100 :: DG180 : ? :: KP210 : RI105

SOLUTION

• Rule (1st→2nd): new 1st letter = old 2nd letter + 2; new 2nd letter = old 1st letter - 2; number ÷ 2.

• Check LW200→YJ100: W+2=Y, L-2=J, 200/2=100. ✓ KP210→RI105: P+2=R, K-2=I, 210/2=105. ✓

• Apply to DG180: G(7)+2 = 9 = I, D(4)-2 = 2 = B, 180/2 = 90 → IB90.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

SHORT TRICK

• Swap the two letters, then +2 on the (new) first and -2 on the (new) second, and halve the number.

NOTE

• Handle letters and the number as separate rules; here the number simply halves.

question:
Select the option that is related to the fourth letter-number cluster in the same way as the first letter-number cluster is related to the second letter-number cluster and fifth letter-number cluster is related to sixth letter-number cluster.

(NOTE: Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking down the numbers into its constituent digits. E.g.13 – Operations on 13 such as adding /subtracting /multiplying etc. to 13 can be performed. Breaking down 13 into 1 and 3 and then performing mathematical operations on 1 and 3 is not allowed)

KFC92 : ADI184 :: ? : KRP202 :: ZXT81 : RVX162
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. RTM101.

GIVEN

• KFC92 : ADI184 :: ? : KRP202 :: ZXT81 : RVX162

SOLUTION

• Rule (1st→2nd): reverse the three letters, subtract 2 from each, and double the number.

• Check KFC92: reverse = CFK = (3,6,11), each -2 = (1,4,9) = ADI, 92×2 = 184. ✓ ZXT81 → RVX162 similarly. ✓

• The needed cluster relates to KRP202 the same way, i.e. reverse-and-(-2) of the answer = KRP: KRP = (11,18,16); add 2 = (13,20,18) = MTR; reverse = RTM. Number 202/2 = 101.

• Answer = RTM101.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

SHORT TRICK

• Forward test the options: reverse RTM = MTR, each -2 = KRP, 101×2 = 202 = KRP202. ✓

NOTE

• 'Reverse letters + fixed shift' is a common SSC coding twist; always test both directions.

question:
Select the option that is related to the fourth number in the same way as the first number is related to the second number and fifth number is related to sixth number.

(NOTE: Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking down the numbers into its constituent digits. E.g.13 – Operations on 13 such as adding /subtracting /multiplying etc. to 13 can be performed. Breaking down 13 into 1 and 3 and then performing mathematical operations on 1 and 3 is not allowed)

4745 : 4786 :: ? : 398 :: 5650 : 5691
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. 357.

GIVEN

• 4745 : 4786 :: ? : 398 :: 5650 : 5691

SOLUTION

• Rule (1st→2nd): add 41. Check 4745+41 = 4786 ✓ and 5650+41 = 5691 ✓.

• So ? + 41 = 398 → ? = 398 - 41 = 357.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

SHORT TRICK

• Constant difference = 41; subtract it from 398.

NOTE

• Find the fixed gap from a clear pair, then apply/invert it on the unknown pair.

question:
Select the option that is related to the second number in the same way as the third number is related to the fourth number and fifth number is related to sixth number.

(NOTE: Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking down the numbers into its constituent digits. E.g.13 – Operations on 13 such as adding /subtracting /multiplying etc. to 13 can be performed. Breaking down 13 into 1 and 3 and then performing mathematical operations on 1 and 3 is not allowed)

? : 841 :: 128 : 357 :: 854 : 1083
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. 612.

GIVEN

• ? : 841 :: 128 : 357 :: 854 : 1083

SOLUTION

• Rule (1st→2nd): add 229. Check 128+229 = 357 ✓ and 854+229 = 1083 ✓.

• So ? + 229 = 841 → ? = 841 - 229 = 612.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

SHORT TRICK

• Difference is fixed at 229; subtract from 841.

NOTE

• 357-128 = 1083-854 = 229 confirms the constant before you solve.

question: In a certain coded language 'DUSKY' is coded as 'FZQHT' and 'BURLY' is coded as 'DZPIT'. How will 'AMAZE' be coded in the same code language?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. CRYWZ.

GIVEN

• DUSKY → FZQHT, BURLY → DZPIT.

SOLUTION

• Position-wise shifts are +2, +5, -2, -3, -5. Check DUSKY: D+2=F, U+5=Z, S-2=Q, K-3=H, Y-5=T. ✓ Same for BURLY→DZPIT.

• AMAZE: A+2=C, M+5=R, A-2=Y (cyclic), Z-3=W, E-5=Z (cyclic) → CRYWZ.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

SHORT TRICK

• Memorise the shift pattern +2, +5, -2, -3, -5 and apply letter by letter.

NOTE

• Wrap around the alphabet: A-2 = Y, E-5 = Z (cyclic subtraction).

question: In a certain code language, 'CAGE' is coded as '95' and 'PURSE' is coded as '59'. How will 'ROAD' be coded in that code language?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. 73.

GIVEN

• CAGE → 95, PURSE → 59.

SOLUTION

• Use reverse alphabetical values (A=26, B=25, …, Z=1) i.e. value = 27 - position, then add 3.

• CAGE: 24+26+20+22 = 92, +3 = 95. ✓ PURSE: 11+6+9+8+22 = 56, +3 = 59. ✓

• ROAD: R=9, O=12, A=26, D=23 → 70, +3 = 73.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

SHORT TRICK

• Reverse-alphabet sum of the word, then +3 gives the code.

NOTE

• Reverse value of a letter = 27 minus its normal position (A=1 … Z=26).

question:
A series is given with one term wrong. Select that wrong term from the given alternatives.

WP76, SU170, QZ264, NE358, KJ452, HO546
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. SU170.

GIVEN

• WP76, SU170, QZ264, NE358, KJ452, HO546

SOLUTION

• 1st letters should fall by 3: W(23), T(20), Q(17), N(14), K(11), H(8). The 2nd term should start with T, but it is S.

• 2nd letters +5 each: P, U, Z, E, J, O ✓. Numbers +94 each: 76, 170, 264, 358, 452, 546 ✓.

• Hence the wrong term is SU170 (should be TU170).

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

SHORT TRICK

• Only the first-letter chain breaks: W-T-Q-N-K-H drops 3 each, so 'S' is the odd one out.

NOTE

• Check each component (1st letter, 2nd letter, number) as its own series to spot the defect.

question:
A series is given with one term missing. Select the correct alternative from the given ones that will complete the series.

MUK77, OWM234, ?, SAQ548, UCS705
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. QYO391.

GIVEN

• MUK77, OWM234, ?, SAQ548, UCS705

SOLUTION

• 1st letters +2: M, O, Q, S, U → Q. 2nd letters +2: U, W, Y, A, C → Y. 3rd letters +2: K, M, O, Q, S → O.

• Numbers +157 each: 77, 234, 391, 548, 705 → 391.

• Missing term = QYO391.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

SHORT TRICK

• Every letter steps +2 and the number steps +157; fill the middle as Q, Y, O, 391.

NOTE

• Split alphanumeric series into three letter-columns and one number-column, each with its own step.
